kill_fact: There is no binding, dated event that pays MP Materials a defined sum; the claimed $35 floor does not exist; and the $82 target capitalises EBITDA the company has contractually shared away. ON THE CATALYST: the only hard date is the 1 January 2027 DFARS restriction (10 U.S.C. 4872 / Section 844 of the FY2021 NDAA), an industry-wide procurement rule that pays MP nothing directly -- and it is not the start of a ban but the widening of one already in force, since DFARS 252.225-7052 has barred magnets 'melted or produced' in a covered country through 31 December 2026, with 1 January 2027 merely extending coverage upstream to mining, refining and separation. The clause keeps live escape valves with no expiration -- nonavailability determinations where compliant material cannot be procured at reasonable prices, the COTS carve-out, electronic devices, and NdFeB made from recycled material milled and sintered in the United States -- so the same shortage of compliant supply that once moved the date can now be handled administratively, contract by contract, without a dollar reaching MP. The company's own milestone has no date at all: the Q1 2026 release confirms NdFeB manufacturing commenced in December 2025 but gives no first finished-magnet revenue date, no GM qualification milestone and no committed date for the Independence 1,000t nameplate, Apple shipments or 10X commissioning. The one company event that IS dated -- Q2 results after the close on 6 August 2026 -- is an earnings print, not a payout. Note also that the real event already FIRED: the July 2025 DoD partnership took the stock from roughly $30 to $100.25 and the entire re-rate has round-tripped to $42.87 (close, 27 July 2026). ON THE FLOOR: nothing backstops the price. Against ~199m diluted shares, net cash is roughly $3.50-3.70 a share and common book equity roughly $11; free cash flow is negative with 2026 capex guided to $500-600m and $1.25bn of 10X spend still ahead; and the July 2025 agreements carry a live commitment for UP TO $350m of ADDITIONAL Series A preferred ranking ahead of the common. The DoD's $30.03 conversion and warrant strike is a cost basis, not a bid, and the $110/kg NdPr floor protects cash flow, not the share price. The stock printed a fresh 52-week low of $41.12 on 24 July 2026 against a $100.25 high, with no structural support within 50% below the market. ON THE NUMBERS: under the DoD offtake the government takes the first $30m of 10X EBITDA above the $140m guarantee and 50% of everything above $170m, and once 10X reaches full production capacity MP owes DoD 30% of the NdPr price above $110/kg. The state both floors 10X and caps it -- so management's $650m medium-term EBITDA is not MP's to capitalise at 20x, and the $82 target is built on economics that have been contracted away. An event-driven special situation needs a hard date, a defined payout and a bounded loss. This has none of the three; it is a production ramp wearing an event's clothes.
corrections: MATERIAL 1 -- The downside floor. The board's $35 is unverifiable and must be struck; no asset, cash balance or contract sits there, and the file's own $32 is a chart level dressed as a floor. Verified structural markers only: common book equity ~$11/share, net cash ~$3.50-3.70/share, DoD conversion/warrant strike $30.03. A de-rating toward an ordinary materials multiple with the construction cushion spent lands nearer $20 than $32. MATERIAL 2 -- The 6 August print setup is INVERTED in dated_milestone, forcing_function and valley_of_death, all of which rest on 'NdPr traded above the $110/kg floor for most of the second quarter, so the $42.3m top-up should shrink sharply or vanish.' The benchmark path says otherwise: roughly $126/kg on 1 April 2026, high-$90s in early May, a trough near $90/kg on 1 June, $109.55/kg at the June benchmark, and only $133.02/kg on 1 JULY -- i.e. at or below the floor through most of Q2, with the quarter's volume-weighted average at or under $110. The Price Protection Agreement settles on a Benchmark Quarterly Average Volume Weighted Price, so the top-up is more likely to persist than to vanish in the August print. The Q2 risk is not 'a good business printing a bad headline'; it is another quarter proving the paying customer is the taxpayer. The above-floor print is a Q3 2026 event, not a Q2 one. MATERIAL 3 -- MP does not 'keep 70% of the excess' today. Per the filed 8-K, DoD's 30% share of price above $110/kg begins ONLY after the 10X Facility reaches full production capacity, i.e. 2028 at the earliest; today MP keeps 100% of the excess and simply receives no top-up. bull_thesis and forcing_function state 70% and are wrong near-term and incomplete long-term. MATERIAL 4 -- sop_bull and target_px of $82 model no government claw-back on 10X: the first $30m of EBITDA above the $140m guarantee goes to DoD, then 50/50 above $170m, with the guarantee escalating 2% a year. Capitalising the full $650m at 20x credits MP with EBITDA it has contracted away; at, say, $300m of 10X EBITDA, MP retains roughly $205m of it. MATERIAL 5 -- The disarming mechanism named in the bear case is the wrong one. 'The deadline has slipped once and can slip again' is right on conclusion, wrong on mechanism: the slip from 1 January 2026 to 1 January 2027 was statutory (Section 854 of the FY2024 NDAA), but no further statutory extension has been enacted and the DFARS clause as currently published still reads 1 January 2027. The realistic route to a quiet disarming is administrative -- nonavailability determinations and the COTS / electronic-device carve-outs -- not another act of Congress. Either way it pays MP nothing. MATERIAL 6 -- An omitted dilution vector: beyond the $400m Series A convertible preferred, the July 2025 agreements include a commitment for UP TO $350m of ADDITIONAL Series A preferred, and the $1.0bn JPMorgan/Goldman 10X facility is 'subject to customary terms and conditions', i.e. not drawn-and-certain. The common sits behind a live and expandable preferred claim, making the floor weaker than even the bear case allows. MINOR 7 -- PPA income of $42.3m is a SEPARATE reported line outside the $90.6m of revenue (combined $132.9m), and the $36.7m figure in the release is Materials-segment adjusted EBITDA; 'strip the top-up out and the quarter was a ~$6m loss' is a defensible inference, not a reported figure, and should be labelled as such. MINOR 8 -- China's MOFCOM listing is dated 22 June 2026, effective immediately, but its practical bite is smaller than the dossier weights it: contemporaneous reporting notes both listed US rare-earth companies say they had already largely cut off Chinese equipment and material supply, so the 10X procurement squeeze is softer than 'management has not addressed it on the record' implies. MINOR 9 -- INSIDER SELLING RE-DATED, AND THE SIGNAL IS WEAKER THAN FRAMED. Form 4 filings show Litinsky's trust selling across 2026: 300,000 shares on 7-8 January for $19.25m, 300,000 in April, 300,000 on 12-13 May at roughly $64-67, 400,000 on 27-29 May in the mid-$60s, and 185,167 on 3 June -- about 1.49m shares, more than the ~1.2m in the file, and the file's 'January to early June' window is CORRECT (an earlier skeptic pass that re-dated the start to 17 April was wrong). Crucially, the filings state the sales were effected pursuant to a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan, and he retains ~11.79m shares. Pre-scheduled sales by a founder who keeps a ~$500m stake are not the discretionary dump the positioning_washout section implies -- keep the fact, discount the inference. MINOR 10 -- 'The sell-side has not moved' is half right: the absence of a downgrade is real, but the street is actively defending the name into the decline (Barclays kept a positive rating while cutting to $65 on 16 July 2026). Unrevised targets are unpriced downside; do not characterise them as neglect. CONFIRMED WITHOUT CHANGE -- Q1 2026 figures tie to the company release (revenue $90.6m, PPA income $42.3m, NdPr production 917t, sales 1,006t, total REO 12,983t, magnetics revenue $21.1m); the DoD terms ($400m preferred and warrant both struck at $30.03 covering up to 11,201,659 shares, 15% as-converted, ten-year $110/kg NdPr floor, $150m heavy-rare-earth loan, $1.0bn JPMorgan/Goldman 10X financing, 7,000tpa 10X to ~10,000tpa total US capacity commissioning 2028, 100% offtake for ten years, $140m minimum annual 10X EBITDA); the 1 January 2027 DFARS effective date and its prior slip from 1 January 2026; the Q2 print after the close on 6 August 2026, announced 16 July 2026; and the tape (52-week range $41.12-$100.25, close $42.87 on 27 July 2026 versus the file's $43.13 live price).
evidence: MP Materials investor press release and Form 8-K, 10 July 2025 (DoD partnership; SEC accession 0001193125-25-157310): $400m Series A convertible preferred at a $30.03 conversion price plus a ten-year warrant for up to 11,201,659 shares struck at $30.03 (together 15% as-converted/as-exercised, subject to a 19.9% cap); a commitment for UP TO $350m of ADDITIONAL Series A preferred; a $150m DoD loan for heavy rare-earth separation; $1.0bn of JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs financing for the 10X Facility; and a ten-year Price Protection Agreement under which DoD pays quarterly the shortfall between $110/kg and the Benchmark Quarterly Average Volume Weighted Price for NdPr produced, with DoD entitled to 30% of the excess above $110/kg ONLY 'after the 10X Facility reaches full production capacity'. The 10X offtake commits DoD to buy 100% of the 7,000tpa output for ten years post-construction and guarantees at least $140m of annual EBITDA, with DoD taking the first $30m of EBITDA above $140m and 50% of amounts above $170m. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1801368/000119312525157310/d43796d8k.htm and https://mpmaterials.com/news/mp-materials-announces-transformational-public-private-partnership-with-the-department-of-defense-to-accelerate-u-s-rare-earth-magnet-independence/

DFARS 252.225-7052 (Acquisition.gov) and the DoD final rule published 30 May 2024 (DFARS Case 2021-D015, Federal Register), implementing Section 844 of the FY2021 NDAA as amended by Section 854 of the FY2024 NDAA: through 31 December 2026 the restriction covers only material melted or produced in China, Russia, Iran or North Korea; effective 1 January 2027 it extends to the entire chain -- mining, refining, separation, melting and production. Section 854 is what moved the effective date from 1 January 2026 to 1 January 2027, expressly to give contractors time to find alternative suppliers. Exceptions surviving into 2027 include COTS items (unless 50%+ covered material by weight), electronic devices, NdFeB made from recycled material milled and sintered in the US, and nonavailability determinations -- the last with no stated expiration. https://www.acquisition.gov/dfars/252.225-7052-restriction-acquisition-certain-magnets-tantalum-and-tungsten. and https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/05/30/2024-11513/defense-federal-acquisition-regulation-supplement-restriction-on-certain-metal-products-dfars-case
